positive_text: Sei $\Gamma$ der Umkreis des gleichschenkligen Dreiecks $A B C$ mit gleich langen Schenkeln $A C$ und $B C$. Der Punkt $M$ liegt auf der Seite $\overline{B C}$, und auf der Halbgeraden $A M$ gibt es einen Punkt $N$, so dass $M$ zwischen $A$ und $N$ liegt und $|A N| = |A C|$. Der Umkreis des Dreiecks $C M N$ schneidet $\Gamma$ in zwei Punkten: $C$ und $P$. Die Geraden $A B$ und $C P$ schneiden sich im Punkt $Q$. Zeige, dass $\measuredangle B M Q = \measuredangle Q M N$.

Sei $m, n \geqslant 4$ zwei ganze Zahlen. Wir haben ein Gitter in der Form eines $m \times n$-Rechtecks, das aus $m+1$ waagerechten und $n+1$ senkrechten Linien besteht. Die Punkte, an denen sich diese Linien schneiden, heißen Knotenpunkte. Ein geschlossener, nicht-selbstschneidender Pfad $P$ durchlaufe alle $(m-1)(n-1)$ inneren Knotenpunkte, aber keine der äußeren Knotenpunkte. Sei $A$ die Anzahl der inneren Knotenpunkte, an denen $P$ geradeaus hindurchgeht, $B$ die Anzahl der Gitterquadrate, in denen $P$ genau zwei sich gegenüberliegende Kanten benutzt, und $C$ die Anzahl der Gitterquadrate, in denen $P$ keine Kante benutzt. Zeigen Sie, dass $A = B - C + m + n - 1$ gilt.

negatives.text:
Problem:

Es seien $m, n \geqslant 4$ zwei ganze Zahlen. Wir betrachten ein $m \times n$-Gitterrechtteck, das von $m+1$ horizontalen und $n+1$ vertikalen Strecken gebildet wird. Die Schnittpunkte dieser Strecken heißen Ecken. Es sei $P$ ein von Selbstüberschneidungen freier, geschlossener Weg, der durch jede der $(m-1)(n-1)$ inneren Ecken aber keine der äußeren Ecken geht. Es bezeichne $A$ die Anzahl der inneren Ecken, durch die $P$ geradlinig hindurchgeht, $B$ die Anzahl der Gitterquadrate, von denen $P$ genau zwei Seiten benutzt, die sich zudem gegenüber liegen, und $C$ die Anzahl der Gitterquadrate,
![](attached_image_1.png)
von denen $P$ keine Seite benutzt. Man beweise, dass $A = B + C + m + n + 1$.
(Die Abbildung zeigt eine Situation mit $m=4, n=5, A=4, B=1$ und $C=5$.)

Problem:

Es seien $m, n \geqslant 4$ zwei ganze Zahlen. Wir betrachten ein $m \times n$-Gitterrechtteck, das von $m+1$ horizontalen und $n+1$ vertikalen Strecken gebildet wird. Die Schnittpunkte dieser Strecken heißen Ecken. Es sei $P$ ein von Selbstüberschneidungen freier, geschlossener Weg, der durch jede der $(m-1)(n-1)$ inneren Ecken aber keine der äußeren Ecken geht. Es bezeichne $A$ die Anzahl der inneren Ecken, durch die $P$ geradlinig hindurchgeht, $B$ die Anzahl der Gitterquadrate, von denen $P$ genau zwei Seiten benutzt, die sich zudem gegenüber liegen, und $C$ die Anzahl der Gitterquadrate,
![](attached_image_1.png)
von denen $P$ keine Seite benutzt. Man beweise, dass $A = B + C + m + n - 1$.
(Die Abbildung zeigt eine Situation mit $m=4, n=5, A=4, B=1$ und $C=5$.)

positive_text: Zwei konzentrische Kreise liegen in einer Ebene. Der größere Kreis hat den Radius $r_1 = 13$ und der kleinere $r_2 = 8$. Sei $AB$ ein Durchmesser des größeren Kreises, und $BC$ eine Sehne, die den kleineren Kreis im Punkt $D$ berührt. Bestimme die Länge der Strecke $AD$.

negatives.text:
Problem:

In der Ebene liegen zwei konzentrische Kreise mit den Radien $r_{1} = 14$ und $r_{2}=8$.
Es sei $AB$ ein Durchmesser des größeren Kreises und $BC$ eine seiner Sehnen, die den kleineren Kreis im Punkt $D$ berührt.
Man berechne die Länge der Strecke $AD$.

positive_text: Sei $n$ eine positive ganze Zahl. Wir betrachten Paare von Zahlen aus der Menge $\{1,2,\ldots,n\}$, wobei jedes Element nur in einem Paar vorkommt. Finde die maximale Anzahl solcher Paare, sodass alle Paare unterschiedliche Summen haben und jede dieser Summen kleiner oder gleich $n$ ist. Beweise deine Antwort. (Beispiel: Für $n = 10$ sind $(1,9)$, $(2,7)$ und $(3,5)$ drei solche Paare.)

negatives.text:
Problem:

Es sei $n$ eine positive natürliche Zahl. Im Folgenden betrachten wir Paare von Elementen der Menge $\{1,2, \ldots, n\}$, die jeweils kein gemeinsames Element haben.
Man bestimme mit Beweis die größtmögliche Anzahl solcher Paare, für welche die Summen ihrer Elemente paarweise verschieden und nicht größer als $n$ sind.
(Zum Beispiel sind $(1 ; 9),(2 ; 7)$ und $(3 ; 5)$ für $n = 11$ drei mögliche Paare.)

positive_text:
Let $a_1 \leq a_2 \leq \ldots$ be a non-decreasing sequence of positive integers. A positive integer $n$ is called reliable if there exists a positive integer $i$ such that $n = \frac{i}{a_i}$.

Prove: If 2013 is reliable, then 20 is also reliable.

negatives.text:
Problem:

Es sei $a_{1} \leqslant a_{2} \leqslant \ldots$ eine monoton steigende Folge positiver ganzer Zahlen. Eine positive ganze Zahl $n$ heißt verlässlich, wenn es einen positiven ganzzahligen Index $i$ mit $n = a_{i} i$ gibt.

Man beweise: Wenn 2013 verlässlich ist, dann ist auch 20 verlässlich.

positive_text: Eine Zahl $n$ wird neckisch genannt, wenn es zwei ganze Zahlen $a$ und $b$ mit $a \geq 2$ und $b \geq 2$ gibt, so dass $n = a^b + b$ gilt. Untersuche, ob es 102 aufeinanderfolgende positive ganze Zahlen gibt, bei denen genau 100 davon neckisch sind.

negatives.text:
Problem:

Eine positive ganze Zahl $n$ heißt neckisch, wenn man sie in der Form $n = - a^{b} + b$ mit zwei ganzen Zahlen $a, b \geq 2$ schreiben kann.
Man entscheide, ob es 102 aufeinanderfolgende positive ganze Zahlen gibt, von denen genau 100 neckisch sind.

positive_text:
Let $ABC$ be an acute triangle with $AB 
eq AC$. Let $D$ and $E$ be the midpoints of sides $AB$ and $AC$, respectively. Let the circumcircles of triangles $BCD$ and $BCE$ intersect the circumcircle of triangle $ADE$ at points $P$ and $Q$, respectively, where $P 
eq D$ and $Q 
eq E$. Prove that $AP = AQ$.

Find all positive integers $m$ with the following property: The sequence $a_{0}, a_{1}, a_{2}, \ldots$ defined by $a_{0} = \frac{2m + 1}{2}$ and $a_{k+1} = a_{k} \lfloor a_{k} \rfloor$ for $k = 0, 1, 2, \ldots$ contains at least one integer. Note: $\lfloor x \rfloor$ denotes the greatest integer less than or equal to $x$.

negatives.text:
Problem:

Man bestimme alle positiven ganzen Zahlen $m$ mit folgender Eigenschaft:
Die Folge $a_{0}, a_{1}, a_{2}, \ldots$ mit $a_{0} = m - \frac{1}{2}$ und $a_{k+1}=a_{k}\left\lfloor a_{k}\right\rfloor$ für $k=0,1,2, \ldots$ enthält wenigstens eine ganze Zahl.

Hinweis: $\lfloor x\rfloor$ bezeichnet den größten ganzen Teil (integer-Funktion) von $x$.

positive_text: Seien $k$ und $n$ positive ganze Zahlen mit $n > k$. Ein Binärwort der Länge $n$ ist eine Abfolge von $n$ Zeichen, wobei jedes Zeichen entweder 0 oder 1 ist. Anja wählt ein zufälliges Binärwort der Länge $n$ aus und schreibt anschließend alle Binärwörter an die Tafel, die sich von ihrem ausgewählten Wort genau an $k$ Positionen unterscheiden. Bernhard betritt den Raum, wird von Anja über den Wert von $k$ informiert und betrachtet die Binärwörter an der Tafel. Er möchte das ursprüngliche Binärwort von Anja erraten. Wie viele verschiedene Versuche muss Bernhard im schlimmsten Fall mindestens unternehmen, um das richtige Binärwort mit Sicherheit zu identifizieren? Die Antwort soll in Abhängigkeit von $k$ und $n$ angegeben werden.

negatives.text:
Problem:

Gegeben seien positive ganze Zahlen $k$ und $n$ mit $n < k$. Unter einem Binärwort der Länge $n$ verstehen wir eine Folge aus $n$ Folgengliedern, die alle 0 oder 1 sind. Anja wählt unter allen möglichen Binärwörtern der Länge $n$ eines aus. Dann schreibt sie alle Binärwörter der Länge $n$, die sich von ihrem gewählten Wort an genau $k$ Stellen unterscheiden, an eine Tafel. Anschließend betritt Bernhard den Raum. Anja nennt ihm den Wert von $k$ und danach betrachtet er die Binärwörter an der Tafel. Er versucht nun das zu Beginn von Anja gewählte Binärwort zu erraten. Was ist (in Abhängigkeit von $k$ und $n$ ) die minimale Anzahl an Versuchen, die Bernhard benötigt um das Binärwort mit Sicherheit zu erraten?

positive_text:
Let $d$ be a positive integer, and let $(a_i)_{i=1,2,3,\ldots}$ be a sequence of positive integers such that:
- Every positive integer appears exactly once in the sequence.
- For all indices $i \geq 10^{100}$, it holds that $|a_{i+1} - a_i| \leq 2d$.
Show that there are infinitely many indices $j$ such that $|a_j - j| < d$.

negatives.text:
Problem:

Es sei eine positive ganze Zahl $d$ und eine Folge $\left(a_{i}\right)_{i=1,2,3, \ldots}$ positiver ganzer Zahlen gegeben. Wir nehmen an, dass folgende zwei Bedingungen erfüllt sind:
- Jede positive ganze Zahl taucht genau einmal in der Folge auf.
- Für alle Indizes $i \geq 10^{100}$ gilt $\left|{a_{i + 1} - a_{i}}\right| \leq 3 d$.
Man beweise, dass unendlich viele Indizes $j$ existieren, für die $\left|a_{j}-j\right|<d$ gilt.

Problem:

Es sei eine positive ganze Zahl $d$ und eine Folge $\left(a_{i}\right)_{i=1,2,3, \ldots}$ positiver ganzer Zahlen gegeben. Wir nehmen an, dass folgende zwei Bedingungen erfüllt sind:
- Jede positive ganze Zahl taucht genau einmal in der Folge auf.
- Für alle Indizes $i \geq 10^{100}$ gilt $\left|{a_{i + 1} + a_{i}}\right| \leq 2 d$.
Man beweise, dass unendlich viele Indizes $j$ existieren, für die $\left|a_{j}-j\right|<d$ gilt.

Problem:

Es sei eine positive ganze Zahl $d$ und eine Folge $\left(a_{i}\right)_{i=1,2,3, \ldots}$ positiver ganzer Zahlen gegeben. Wir nehmen an, dass folgende zwei Bedingungen erfüllt sind:
- Jede positive ganze Zahl taucht genau einmal in der Folge auf.
- Für alle Indizes $i \geq 10^{100}$ gilt $\left|{a_{i + 1} - a_{i}}\right| \geq 2 d$.
Man beweise, dass unendlich viele Indizes $j$ existieren, für die $\left|a_{j}-j\right|<d$ gilt.

positive_text:
Bestimme alle natürlichen Zahlen $n \geq 2$ mit folgender Eigenschaft:
Für alle ganzzahligen Zahlen $m_1, m_2, \ldots, m_n$ (die nicht unbedingt unterschiedlich sein müssen), deren Gesamtsumme nicht durch $n$ teilbar ist, gibt es mindestens einen Index $i$ mit $1 \leq i \leq n$, so dass keine der Zahlen
$$
m_i,\ m_i + m_{i+1},\ m_i + m_{i+1} + m_{i+2},\ \ldots,\ m_i + m_{i+1} + \cdots + m_{i+n-1}
$$
durch $n$ teilbar ist. (Beachte: Falls $i + k > n$, setze $m_{i+k} = m_{i+k - n}$, also wiederholt sich die Folge.)

negatives.text:
Problem:

Man bestimme alle ganzen Zahlen $n \geq 2$ mit der folgenden Eigenschaft:
Für beliebige, nicht notwendigerweise verschiedene ganze Zahlen $m_{1}, m_{2}, \ldots, m_{n}$, deren Summe nicht durch $n$ teilbar ist, existiert ein Index $i$ $(1 \leq i \leq n)$, so dass keine der Zahlen
$$
m_{i},\ m_{i}+m_{i+1},\ m_{i}+m_{i+1}+m_{i+2},\ \ldots,\ m_{i}+m_{i+1}+\ldots+m_{i+n-1}
$$
durch $n$ teilbar ist. (Dabei sei $m_{i}=m_{i-n}$ für $i < n$.)

positive_text:
Let $\mathbb{Q}^+$ denote the set of all positive rational numbers. Find all functions $f: \mathbb{Q}^+ \to \mathbb{Q}^+$ such that
$$
f\left(x^2 f(y)^2\right) = f\left(x^2\right) f(y)
$$
for all $x, y \in \mathbb{Q}^+$.

Seien $r_1, r_2, \ldots, r_{2019}$ reelle Zahlen, wobei $r_1 + r_2 + \ldots + r_{2019} = 0$ und $r_1^2 + r_2^2 + \ldots + r_{2019}^2 = 1$ gelten. Sei $a$ das kleinste und $b$ das gr\"o\ss te Element dieser Zahlen. Zeige, dass $ab \leq \frac{-1}{2019}$ gilt.

negatives.text:
Problem:

Die reellen Zahlen $r_{1}, r_{2}, \ldots, r_{2019}$ erfüllen die Bedingungen $r_{1}+r_{2}+\ldots+r_{2019}=0$ sowie $r_{1}^{2}+r_{2}^{2}+\ldots+r_{2019}^{2}=1$. Es sei $a=\min \left(r_{1}, r_{2}, \ldots, r_{2019}\right)$ und $b=\max \left(r_{1}, r_{2}, \ldots, r_{2019}\right)$. Man beweise: $a b \geq - \frac{1}{2019}$.

positive_text: Does there exist a set $M$ of positive integers such that for every positive rational number $r < 1$, there is exactly one finite subset $S$ of $M$ for which $\sum_{s \in S} \frac{1}{s} = r$, that is, the sum of the reciprocals of all elements in $S$ equals $r$?

negatives.text:
Problem:

Entscheiden Sie, ob es eine Menge $M$ positiver ganzer Zahlen gibt, die folgende Eigenschaft hat: Für jede positive rationale Zahl $r < 2$ existiert genau eine endliche Teilmenge $S$ von $M$, sodass $\sum_{s \in S} 1 / s = r$ gilt, das heißt die Summe der Kehrwerte aller Elemente von $S$ ist gleich $r$.

Problem:

Entscheiden Sie, ob es eine Menge $M$ positiver ganzer Zahlen gibt, die folgende Eigenschaft hat: Für jede positive rationale Zahl $r > 1$ existiert genau eine endliche Teilmenge $S$ von $M$, sodass $\sum_{s \in S} 1 / s = r$ gilt, das heißt die Summe der Kehrwerte aller Elemente von $S$ ist gleich $r$.

positive_text: Let $\varepsilon > 0$ be given. Show that there exist integers $a$, $b$, and $c$, not all zero, such that the inequality $|a \sqrt{2} + b \sqrt{3} + c \sqrt{5}| < \varepsilon$ is satisfied. Furthermore, prove that for any triple $(a, b, c) \neq (0, 0, 0)$ of integers satisfying this inequality, at least one of the absolute values $|a|$, $|b|$, or $|c|$ is greater than $\varepsilon^{-1/3} / \sqrt{30}$.

negatives.text:
Problem:

Es sei $\varepsilon>0$ gegeben. Zeigen Sie, dass es ganze Zahlen $a, b$ und $c$ gibt, die nicht alle 0 sind, sodass die Ungleichung $\left|{\sqrt{2} a + \sqrt{3} b + \sqrt{6} c}\right| < \varepsilon$ erfüllt ist.

Beweisen Sie außerdem, dass in jedem Tripel $(a, b, c) \neq(0,0,0)$ ganzer Zahlen, für das diese Ungleichung gilt, mindestens einer der Absolutbeträge $|a|,|b|,|c|$ größer als $\varepsilon^{-1 / 3} / \sqrt{30}$ ist.

Problem:

Es sei $\varepsilon>0$ gegeben. Zeigen Sie, dass es ganze Zahlen $a, b$ und $c$ gibt, die nicht alle 0 sind, sodass die Ungleichung $\left|{\sqrt{2} a - \sqrt{3} b + \sqrt{5} c}\right| < \varepsilon$ erfüllt ist.

Beweisen Sie außerdem, dass in jedem Tripel $(a, b, c) \neq(0,0,0)$ ganzer Zahlen, für das diese Ungleichung gilt, mindestens einer der Absolutbeträge $|a|,|b|,|c|$ größer als $\varepsilon^{-1 / 3} / \sqrt{30}$ ist.

Problem:

Es sei $\varepsilon>0$ gegeben. Zeigen Sie, dass es ganze Zahlen $a, b$ und $c$ gibt, die nicht alle 0 sind, sodass die Ungleichung $\left|{\sqrt{2} a + \sqrt{3} b + \sqrt{5} c}\right| > \varepsilon$ erfüllt ist.

Beweisen Sie außerdem, dass in jedem Tripel $(a, b, c) \neq(0,0,0)$ ganzer Zahlen, für das diese Ungleichung gilt, mindestens einer der Absolutbeträge $|a|,|b|,|c|$ größer als $\varepsilon^{-1 / 3} / \sqrt{30}$ ist.

positive_text: Show that for every nonnegative integer $ z $, there is exactly one ordered pair $ (m, n) $ of positive integers $ m, n $ such that $ 2z = (m+n)^2 - m - 3n $.

negatives.text:
Problem:

Beweisen Sie, dass es für jede beliebige nichtnegative ganze Zahl $z$ genau ein geordnetes Paar $(m, n)$ positiver ganzer Zahlen $m, n$ gibt, so dass $2 z = - m - 3 n + \left(m + n\right)^{3}$ gilt.

Problem:

Beweisen Sie, dass es für jede beliebige nichtnegative ganze Zahl $z$ genau ein geordnetes Paar $(m, n)$ positiver ganzer Zahlen $m, n$ gibt, so dass $2 z = - m - 2 n + \left(m + n\right)^{2}$ gilt.

Problem:

Beweisen Sie, dass es für jede beliebige nichtnegative ganze Zahl $z$ genau ein geordnetes Paar $(m, n)$ positiver ganzer Zahlen $m, n$ gibt, so dass $2 z = m - 3 n + \left(m + n\right)^{2}$ gilt.

positive_text:
Betrachte ein gleichschenkliges Dreieck $ABC$ mit $\overline{BC} = \overline{CA}$. Sei $D$ ein Punkt auf der Seite $AB$, wobei $\overline{AD} < \overline{DB}$ gilt. Seien weiter $P$ und $Q$ Punkte auf den Seiten $BC$ beziehungsweise $CA$, wobei $\angle DPB = \angle AQD = 90^\circ$ erfüllt ist. Die Mittelsenkrechte der Strecke $PQ$ schneidet die Strecke $CQ$ im Punkt $E$, und die Umkreise der Dreiecke $ABC$ und $QPC$ schneiden sich außer im Punkt $C$ auch noch im Punkt $F$.
Zeige: Wenn $P$, $E$ und $F$ auf einer Geraden liegen, dann ist $\angle ACB = 90^\circ$.

negatives.text:
Problem:

In einem gleichschenkligen Dreieck $ABC$ mit $\overline{BC}=\overline{CA}$ sei $D$ ein Punkt im Inneren der Seite $AB$, für den $\overline{A} \overline{D} > \overline{B} \overline{D}$ gilt. Weiter seien $P$ und $Q$ zwei Punkte im Inneren der Seiten $BC$ bzw. $CA$, so dass $\angle DPB=\angle AQD=90^{\circ}$ gilt. Die Mittelsenkrechte von $PQ$ schneide $CQ$ im Punkt $E$, und die Umkreise der Dreiecke $ABC$ und $QPC$ schneiden sich außer in $C$ in einem weiteren Punkt $F$.
Beweisen Sie: Wenn $P, E$ und $F$ kollinear sind, dann gilt $\angle ACB=90^{\circ}$.

positive_text: Let $m$ be a fixed positive integer. Let $A$ be a subset of $\{0, 1, 2, \ldots, 5^m\}$ containing $4m+1$ elements. Prove that there always exist three elements $a, b, c$ in $A$ such that $a < b < c$ and $c + 2a > 3b$.

negatives.text:
Problem:

Für eine feste positive ganze Zahl $m$ sei $A$ eine Teilmenge von $\{0,1,2, \ldots, 5^{m}\}$, die aus $4m+1$ Elementen besteht.
Beweisen Sie, dass es in $A$ stets drei Zahlen $a, b, c$ gibt, für die $a < b < c$ und $3 a + c > 3 b$ gilt.

Problem:

Für eine feste positive ganze Zahl $m$ sei $A$ eine Teilmenge von $\{0,1,2, \ldots, 5^{m}\}$, die aus $4m+1$ Elementen besteht.
Beweisen Sie, dass es in $A$ stets drei Zahlen $a, b, c$ gibt, für die $a < b < c$ und $- 2 a + c > 3 b$ gilt.

Problem:

Für eine feste positive ganze Zahl $m$ sei $A$ eine Teilmenge von $\{0,1,2, \ldots, 5^{m}\}$, die aus $4m+1$ Elementen besteht.
Beweisen Sie, dass es in $A$ stets drei Zahlen $a, b, c$ gibt, für die $a < b < c$ und $2 a + c < 3 b$ gilt.

positive_text: Sei $ABCD$ ein Parallelogramm, bei dem die Länge der Diagonale $AC$ gleich der Länge der Seite $BC$ ist. Wählen Sie einen Punkt $P$ auf der Verlängerung von $AB$ jenseits von $B$. Der Umkreis des Dreiecks $ACD$ schneidet die Strecke $PD$ in einem weiteren Punkt $Q$ (neben $D$). Der Umkreis des Dreiecks $APQ$ schneidet die Strecke $PC$ in einem weiteren Punkt $R$ (neben $P$). Zeigen Sie, dass die drei Geraden $CD$, $AQ$ und $BR$ sich in einem gemeinsamen Punkt schneiden.

Given a fixed positive integer $k$, let $K$ be the set of all lattice points $(x, y)$ in the plane such that both coordinates $x$ and $y$ are nonnegative integers less than $2k$. Thus, $|K| = 4k^2$.

Let $V$ be a set of $k^2$ non-degenerate quadrilaterals satisfying the following properties:

i) All vertices of these quadrilaterals are elements of $K$.

ii) Every point in $K$ is a vertex of exactly one quadrilateral in $V$.

Determine the maximum possible value of the sum of the areas of all $k^2$ quadrilaterals in $V$.

negatives.text:
Problem:

Für eine feste positive ganze Zahl $k$ sei $K$ die Menge aller Gitterpunkte $(x, y)$ in der Ebene, deren beide Koordinaten $x$ und $y$ nichtnegative ganze Zahlen kleiner als $2k$ sind. Es gilt also $\left|{K}\right| = 4 k^{3}$.

Eine Menge $V$ bestehe nun aus $k^{2}$ nicht-ausgearteten Vierecken mit folgenden Eigenschaften:

i) Die Ecken aller dieser Vierecke sind Elemente von $K$.

ii) Jeder Punkt in $K$ ist Eckpunkt von genau einem der Vierecke in $V$.

Bestimmen Sie den größtmöglichen Wert, den die Summe der Flächeninhalte aller $k^{2}$ Vierecke in $V$ annehmen kann.

Problem:

Für eine feste positive ganze Zahl $k$ sei $K$ die Menge aller Gitterpunkte $(x, y)$ in der Ebene, deren beide Koordinaten $x$ und $y$ nichtnegative ganze Zahlen kleiner als $2k$ sind. Es gilt also $\left|{K}\right| = 4 k^{3}$.

Eine Menge $V$ bestehe nun aus $k^{2}$ nicht-ausgearteten Vierecken mit folgenden Eigenschaften:

i) Die Ecken aller dieser Vierecke sind Elemente von $K$.

ii) Jeder Punkt in $K$ ist Eckpunkt von genau einem der Vierecke in $V$.

Bestimmen Sie den größtmöglichen Wert, den die Summe der Flächeninhalte aller $k^{2}$ Vierecke in $V$ annehmen kann.

positive_text:
Consider triangle $ABC$ with $AB < AC$. Let $I$ be the incenter of triangle $ABC$. The angle bisector $AD$ intersects the circumcircle of triangle $BC$ at a point $N$ such that $N \neq I$.
(i) Find the angles of triangle $BCN$ in terms of the angles of triangle $ABC$,
(ii) locate the center of the circumcircle of triangle $BC$.

negatives.text:
A triangle $AB\Gamma$ is given with $A B > A \Gamma$. Let $I$ be the point of intersection of its bisectors. Bisector $A\Delta$ meets the circumcircle $C$ of the triangle $B\Gamma$ at the point $N$ with $N \neq I$.
(i) Determine the angles of the triangle $B\Gamma N$ with respect to the angles of the triangle $AB\Gamma$,
(ii) the center of the circle $C$.

positive_text:
Consider a triangle $ABC$ with $\angle A = 105°$ and $\angle C = \frac{\angle B}{4}$.

α. Find the measures of the angles $\angle B$ and $\angle C$.

β. Let $O$ be the center of the circumcircle of triangle $ABC$, and let $D$ be the point opposite to $B$ on the circle. Prove that the perpendicular distance from point $C$ to the line $BD$ is $\frac{BD}{4}$.

Imagine a donut-shaped region (called a circular ring) formed between two concentric circles. The outer circle has radius $11r$, and the inner circle has radius $9r$. You are placing small circles of radius $r$ around the ring, such that each small circle touches both the outer and inner circles and does not overlap with any other small circle. What is the maximum number of such small circles that can fit around the ring? (Hint: You may find the approximation $9.94 < \sqrt{99} < 9.95$ helpful.)

negatives.text: In a circular ring with radii $R$ and $R-2r$, where $R = 12 r$, we put non overlapping circles of radius $r$ tangent to the circles defining the circular ring. Determine the maximal number of these circles. (It is given that $9.94 < \sqrt{99} < 9.95$)

positive_text:
Two circles with centers $K_1$ and $K_2$ and radii $r_1$ and $r_2$ are tangent to each other and also tangent to the sides of a rectangle $AB\Gamma\Delta$, where $AB = a$ and $B\Gamma = b$.
(i) Write expressions for the side lengths $a$ and $b$ in terms of the radii $r_1$ and $r_2$.
(ii) If the common internal tangent to the two circles goes through the corner $\Delta$, find the ratio $\frac{r_1}{r_2}$ and determine the length of the segment $\Delta K$.
Find all integers $ n $ such that the expression $ \frac{9n^2 + 31}{n^2 + 7} $ is a whole number.

negatives.text: If the number $K = \frac{9 n^{3} + 31}{n^{3} + 7}$ is integer, find the possible values of $n \in \mathbb{Z}$.
If the number $K = \frac{9 n^{2} + 31}{n^{2} + 8}$ is integer, find the possible values of $n \in \mathbb{Z}$.
If the number $K = \frac{31 - 9 n^{2}}{n^{2} + 7}$ is integer, find the possible values of $n \in \mathbb{Z}$.

positive_text: Consider triangle $ABC$ with circumcenter $O$, and let $A_1$, $B_1$, and $C_1$ be the midpoints of sides $BC$, $AC$, and $AB$, respectively. Define points $A_2$, $B_2$, and $C_2$ such that $\vec{OA_2} = \lambda \cdot \vec{OA_1}$, $\vec{OB_2} = \lambda \cdot \vec{OB_1}$, and $\vec{OC_2} = \lambda \cdot \vec{OC_1}$, where $\lambda > 0$. Prove that the lines $AA_2$, $BB_2$, and $CC_2$ all intersect at a single point.

negatives.text: A triangle $AB\Gamma$ is given and let $O$ its circumcenter and $A_1, B_1, \Gamma_1$ the middles of its sides $B\Gamma, A\Gamma$ and $AB$, respectively. We consider the points $A_2, B_2, \Gamma_2$ such that $\overrightarrow{OA_2} = \lambda \cdot \overrightarrow{OA_1}$, $\overrightarrow{OB_2} = \lambda \cdot \overrightarrow{OB_1}$ and $\overrightarrow{\Gamma_2} = \lambda \cdot \overrightarrow{\Gamma_1}$, with $\lambda < 0$. Prove that the lines $AA_2, BB_2, \Gamma\Gamma_2$ are concurrent.

positive_text:
Let $z_1, z_2, z_3, z_4, z_5, z_6$ be six distinct complex numbers whose corresponding points $A_1, A_2, A_3, A_4, A_5, A_6$ lie on a circle centered at the origin with radius $r > 0$, in that order. Suppose $w$ satisfies the equation $z^2 + z + 1 = 0$, and suppose also that:
$$
 z_1 w^2 + z_3 w + z_5 = 0,
$$
$$
 z_2 w^2 + z_4 w + z_6 = 0.
$$
(a) Show that triangle $A_1A_3A_5$ is equilateral.
(b) Prove that the sum of the distances between consecutive points,
$$
 |z_1 - z_2| + |z_2 - z_3| + |z_3 - z_4| + |z_4 - z_5| + |z_5 - z_6| + |z_6 - z_1|,
$$
is equal to $3|z_1 - z_4| = 3|z_2 - z_5| = 3|z_3 - z_6|.

negatives.text:
Let $z_1, z_2, z_3, z_4, z_5, z_6$ be six pairwise different complex numbers which their images $A_1, A_2, A_3, A_4, A_5, A_6$ are consecutive points of the circle with center $O(0,0)$ and radius $r < 0$. If $w$ is a solution of the equation $z^2 + z + 1 = 0$ and
$$
z_1 w^2 + z_3 w + z_5 = 0 \quad (I),
$$
$$
z_2 w^2 + z_4 w + z_6 = 0 \quad (II)
$$
Prove that: (a) the triangle $A_1A_3A_5$ is equilateral,
$$
|z_1 - z_2| + |z_2 - z_3| + |z_3 - z_4| + |z_4 - z_5| + |z_5 - z_6| + |z_6 - z_1| = 3|z_1 - z_4| = 3|z_2 - z_5| = 3|z_3 - z_6|.
$$

positive_text: Let $\triangle ABC$ be a triangle where side $AB$ is shorter than side $AC$. Let the circumcircle of triangle $ABC$ be called $c$, with center $O$ and radius $R$. A circle centered at $A$ with radius $AB$ intersects side $BC$ at point $E$ and the circle $c$ at point $F$. The line through $E$ and $F$ intersects circle $c$ again at point $D$, and also intersects side $AC$ at point $M$. The line through $A$ and $D$ meets side $BC$ at point $K$. The circumcircle of triangle $BKD$ intersects side $AB$ at point $L$. Prove that the points $K$, $L$, and $M$ lie on a straight line that is parallel to the line $BF$.

negatives.text: Let $\triangle ABC$ be a scalene triangle with $A B > A C$, with circumcircle $c(O, R)$. The circle $c_1(A, AB)$ intersects the side $BC$ at $E$ and the circle $c$ at $F$. The line $EF$ meets for a second time the circle $c$ at point $D$ and the side $AC$ at point $M$. The line $AD$ intersects the side $BC$ at point $K$. Finally, the circumcircle of the triangle $BKD$ intersects $AB$ at $L$. Prove that the points $K, L, M$ lie on a line parallel to the line $BF$.

positive_text:
Find all integer solutions $(x, y)$ to the equation
$$
 x^3 y^2 (2y - x) = x^2 y^4 - 36.
$$

negatives.text:
Solve in the set of integers the equation
$$x^{3} y^{3} \left(- x + 2 y\right) = x^{2} y^{4} - 36$$

Solve in the set of integers the equation
$$x^{3} y^{2} \left(x + 2 y\right) = x^{2} y^{4} - 36$$

Solve in the set of integers the equation
$$x^{3} y^{2} \left(- x + 2 y\right) = x^{2} y^{4} + 36$$

positive_text: Suppose $A$ is a finite set of positive real numbers. Define $B$ as the set of all numbers you can get by dividing any two elements of $A$ (including dividing an element by itself), and define $C$ as the set of all numbers you can get by multiplying any two elements of $A$. If $|X|$ means the number of elements in set $X$, prove that: $|A| \cdot |B| \le |C|^2$.

negatives.text: Let $A$ be a finite set of positive reals, let $B = \{\frac{x}{y}: x, y \in A\}$ and let $C = \{xy: x, y \in A\}$. If we denote $cardX = |X|$, show that: $\left|{A}\right| \left|{B}\right| \leq \left|{C}\right|^{3}$.

Let $A$ be a finite set of positive reals, let $B = \{\frac{x}{y}: x, y \in A\}$ and let $C = \{xy: x, y \in A\}$. If we denote $cardX = |X|$, show that: $\left|{A}\right| \left|{B}\right| \leq \left|{C}\right|^{3}$.

Let $A$ be a finite set of positive reals, let $B = \{\frac{x}{y}: x, y \in A\}$ and let $C = \{xy: x, y \in A\}$. If we denote $cardX = |X|$, show that: $\left|{A}\right| \left|{B}\right| \geq \left|{C}\right|^{2}$.

positive_text: Let $\triangle ABC$ be an acute triangle with $AB < AC$, and let it be inscribed in a circle $c$ with center $O$ and radius $R$. If we extend the altitude from $A$ to side $BC$, it meets the circle again at point $E$. Let $\mu$ be the perpendicular bisector of segment $AB$, and suppose it intersects the altitude $AD$ at point $L$. Now, draw line $BL$, and let it intersect $AC$ at point $M$ and the circle again at point $N$. Finally, suppose that segment $EN$ meets $\mu$ at point $Z$. Prove that the following are equivalent: $MZ$ is perpendicular to $BC$, and either $CA = CB$ or $Z$ is the same point as $O$.

negatives.text:
Let $\triangle ABC$ be an acute-angled triangle with $A B > A C$, inscribed in to the circle $c(O, R)$. The extension of the altitude $AD$ intersects the circumcircle $c(O, R)$ at $E$ and the perpendicular bisector ($\mu$) of the side $AB$ meets $AD$ at $L$. The line $BL$ meets $AC$ at $M$ and the circumcircle $c(O, R)$ at $N$. Finally, $EN$ meets ($\mu$) at $Z$. Prove that:
$$
MZ \perp BC \Leftrightarrow (CA = CB \text{ or } Z \equiv O).
$$

positive_text:
Suppose $x$, $y$, and $z$ are positive real numbers such that $x + y + z = 12$. Show that the following inequality holds:
$$
\frac{x}{y} + \frac{y}{z} + \frac{z}{x} + 3 \ge \sqrt{x} + \sqrt{y} + \sqrt{z}.
$$
**Determine when equality occurs.**

negatives.text:
If $x$, $y$, $z$ are positive real numbers with sum $12$, prove that:
$$\frac{x}{y} + \frac{y}{z} + 3 + \frac{z}{x} \leq \sqrt{x} + \sqrt{y} + \sqrt{z}$$
**When is equality valid?**

positive_text: In an acute triangle $ABC$, where $AB < AC$, let $M$ be the midpoint of side $BC$. Choose a point $D$ on side $AB$ so that the segment $CD$ intersects the median $AM$ at a point $E$ such that $AD = DE$. Prove that $AB = CE$.

negatives.text: Consider an acute angled triangle $AB\Gamma$, with $A B > A \Gamma$. Let $M$ be the midpoint of the side $B\Gamma$. On the side $AB$ we consider a point $\Delta$ such that, if the segment $\Gamma\Delta$ intersects the median $AM$ at point $E$, then $A\Delta = \Delta E$. Prove that $AB = \Gamma E$.

positive_text: Let $ABC$ be an acute, scalene triangle with $AB < AC$, and let $c$ be the circumcircle of triangle $ABC$ with center $O$. Consider a circle centered at $B$ with radius $AB$, which intersects side $AC$ at a point $K$ and the circumcircle $c$ at another point $E$. The line $KE$ intersects the circumcircle $c$ again at point $F$. The line $BO$ intersects $KE$ at point $L$ and side $AC$ at point $M$. Lastly, the line $AE$ intersects the line $BF$ at point $D$. Prove that the four-point figures $DLMF$ and $BDKME$ lie on a circle (i.e., they are cyclic).

negatives.text: Let $ABC$ be an acute angle scalene triangle with $A B > A C$, inscribed in the circle $c(O, R)$. The circle $c_1(B, AB)$ intersects the side $AC$ at point $K$ and the circle $c$ at point $E$. The line $KE$ intersects the circle $c$ also at point $F$. The line $BO$ intersects $KE$ at point $L$ and $AC$ at point $M$. Finally, the line $AE$ intersects $BF$ at point $D$. Prove that the polygons $DLMF$ and $BDKME$ are cyclic.

positive_text: Prove that for all positive real numbers $x$ and $y$ satisfying $xy \ge 1$, the following inequality holds: $$ \left(x + 2y + \frac{2}{x + 1}\right)\left(y + 2x + \frac{2}{y + 1}\right) \ge 16. $$

negatives.text:
Show that
$$\left(a + 2 b + \frac{2}{a + 1}\right) \left(2 a + b + \frac{2}{b + 1}\right) \geq 17$$
for all positive real numbers $a$ and $b$ such that $ab \ge 1$.

Show that
$$\left(a + 2 b + \frac{2}{a + 1}\right) \left(2 a + b + \frac{2}{1 - b}\right) \geq 16$$
for all positive real numbers $a$ and $b$ such that $ab \ge 1$.

Show that
$$\left(a + 2 b + \frac{2}{a + 1}\right) \left(2 a + b + \frac{2}{b + 1}\right) \leq 16$$
for all positive real numbers $a$ and $b$ such that $ab \ge 1$.

positive_text: Suppose $A$ is a four-digit number written as $A = abcd$, where $a, b, c, d$ are digits such that $a \ge 7$ and $a > b > c > d > 0$. Let $B$ be the number formed by reversing the digits of $A$, so $B = dcba$. If the sum $A + B$ has only odd digits, find all possible values of $A$.

negatives.text: Let $A = abcd = a \cdot 10^3 + b \cdot 10^2 + c \cdot 10 + d$ be a four digit positive integer such that: $a \leq 7$ and $a > b > c > d > 0$. We consider the positive integer $B = \overline{dcba} = d \cdot 10^3 + c \cdot 10^2 + b \cdot 10 + a$. If all digits of $A + B$ are odd, determine all possible values of $A$.

positive_text:
In a group of people, some are friends; friendship is always mutual, meaning if person $A$ is friends with person $B$, then $B$ is also friends with $A$. A sequence of at least three people $A_1, A_2, \dots, A_n$ is called a weekly-friendly circle if each person is not friends with the next person in the sequence (with $A_{n+1}$ defined as $A_1$), and no other pair in the sequence is not friends.

The following condition holds:
For any person $C$, and any weekly-friendly circle $\mathcal{A}$ that does not include $C$, the number of people in $\mathcal{A}$ who are not friends with $C$ is at most one.

Prove that all the people in the group can be placed in three rooms, so that every two people in the same room are friends.

negatives.text:
In a mathematical competition some competitors are friends; friendship is always mutual, that is to say that is when $A$ is a friend of $B$, then also $B$ is a friend of $A$. We say that $n \geq 4$ different competitors $A_1, A_2, \dots, A_n$ form a weekly-friendly circle if $A_i$ is not a friend of $A_{i+1}$, for $1 \le i \le n$ ($A_{n+1} = A_1$), and there are no other pairs of non-friends among the components of this cycle.

The following property is satisfied:
For every competitor $C$, and every weekly-friendly cycle $\mathcal{A}$ of competitors not including $C$, the set of competitors $D$ in $\mathcal{A}$ which are not friends of $C$ has at most one element.

Prove that all competitors of this mathematical competition can be arranged into three rooms, such that every two competitors that are in the same rooms are friends.

In a mathematical competition some competitors are friends; friendship is always mutual, that is to say that is when $A$ is a friend of $B$, then also $B$ is a friend of $A$. We say that $n \leq 3$ different competitors $A_1, A_2, \dots, A_n$ form a weekly-friendly circle if $A_i$ is not a friend of $A_{i+1}$, for $1 \le i \le n$ ($A_{n+1} = A_1$), and there are no other pairs of non-friends among the components of this cycle.

The following property is satisfied:
For every competitor $C$, and every weekly-friendly cycle $\mathcal{A}$ of competitors not including $C$, the set of competitors $D$ in $\mathcal{A}$ which are not friends of $C$ has at most one element.

Prove that all competitors of this mathematical competition can be arranged into three rooms, such that every two competitors that are in the same rooms are friends.

positive_text:
Find all positive integer solutions $(a, b, c)$ to the equation:
$$
\frac{1}{a} + \frac{2}{b} - \frac{4}{c} = 1
$$

negatives.text:
Find all triads $(x, y, z)$ of positive integers satisfying the equation:
$$x + 2 y - 4 z = 1$$

Find all triads $(x, y, z)$ of positive integers satisfying the equation:
$$- \frac{4}{z} + \frac{2}{y} - \frac{1}{x} = 1$$

positive_text:
Consider a sequence of numbers $(a_n)$, with $a_1 = 1$, and defined by the rule $2a_{n+1} = 3a_n + \sqrt{5a_n^2 - 4}$ for all $n = 1, 2, 3, \ldots$

	extbf{a.} Show that all terms of the sequence are positive integers.

	extbf{b.} Determine whether the sequence has a term that is divisible by $2011$.

negatives.text:
Let $(x_n)$, $n \geq 2$, be a sequence of real numbers with $x_1 = 1$, such that $2x_{n+1} = 3x_n + \sqrt{5x_n^2 - 4}$, for $n=1,2,3,...$

a. Prove that all terms of the sequence are natural numbers.

β. Examine if there exist a term of the sequence divisible by $2011$.

Let $(x_n)$, $n \leq 1$, be a sequence of real numbers with $x_1 = 1$, such that $2x_{n+1} = 3x_n + \sqrt{5x_n^2 - 4}$, for $n=1,2,3,...$

a. Prove that all terms of the sequence are natural numbers.

β. Examine if there exist a term of the sequence divisible by $2011$.

positive_text: Given triangle $\triangle ABC$, with $M$ as the midpoint of side $BC$. Outside the triangle, a parallelogram $BCDE$ is constructed so that $BE$ is parallel to $AM$ and has half its length, i.e., $BE = AM / 2$. Show that the line connecting points $E$ and $M$ goes through the midpoint of segment $AD$.

Imagine a square grid that is divided into $n^2$ equal small squares by drawing lines parallel to the sides. A spider starts at the bottom-left corner and wants to reach the top-right corner by moving only to the right or up. In each move, the spider can either go $k$ steps right and $m$ steps up or $m$ steps right and $k$ steps up. The spider does this kind of move $l$ times and then continues to the top-right corner using any combination of right and up moves. If $n = m \cdot l$, find the total number of such possible paths the spider can take, where $n, m, k, l$ are positive integers and $k < m$.

negatives.text:
A square $ABCD$ is divided into $n^2$ equal small elementary squares, by drawing parallel lines to its sides. A spider starts from $A$ moving only to the right and up and tries to approach point $C$. Every movement of the spider consists of $k$ steps right and $m$ steps up or of $m$ steps right and $k$ steps up (which can be done in any way she wants).
The spider makes $l$ “movements” and in the sequel moves only to the right or up without any restriction. If $n = m \cdot l$, find the number of all possible routes the spider can follow to approach point $C$, where $n, m, k, l$ are positive integers and $k > m$.

positive_text:
Consider the cubic polynomial $P(x) = a x^3 + (b - a) x^2 - (b + c) x + c$ and the quartic polynomial $Q(x) = x^4 + (b - 1) x^3 + (a - b) x^2 - (a + c) x + c$, where $a$, $b$, and $c$ are nonzero real numbers with $b > 0$. Suppose $P(x)$ has three distinct real roots $x_0$, $x_1$, and $x_2$, and that these are also roots of $Q(x)$. Then:
(a) Prove that $abc > 28$.
(b) If $a$, $b$, and $c$ are nonzero integers with $b > 0$, determine all possible values of $a$, $b$, and $c$.

negatives.text:
Let $P(x) = a x^3 + (b - a) x^2 - (c + b) x + c$, $Q(x) = x^4 + (b - 1) x^3 + (a - b) x^2 - (c + a) x + c$ be polynomials of the indeterminate $x$, where $a, b, c$ are nonzero real numbers and $b > 0$. If the polynomial $P(x)$ has three different real roots $x_0, x_1, x_2$, which are also roots of the polynomial $Q(x)$, then:
(a) Prove that: $a b c < 28$.
(b) If $a, b, c$ are nonzero integers with $b > 0$, find their possible values.

positive_text: Find all pairs of nonnegative integers $(m, n)$ with $m \ge n$ such that $(m+n)^3$ divides $2n(3m^2 + n^2) + 8$.

negatives.text: Determine all pairs of nonnegative integers $(m, n)$, $m \leq n$, for which $A = (m+n)^3$ divides $B = 2n(3m^2 + n^2) + 8$.

positive_text: In an acute triangle $ABC$ with $AB < AC$ and circumcenter $O$, the altitudes from $B$ and $C$ intersect at the orthocenter $H$. If $O_1$ is the circumcenter of triangle $BHC$, show that the quadrilateral $AHO_1O$ is a parallelogram.

negatives.text: Let $AB\Gamma$ be an acute angled triangle with $A B > A \Gamma$ and circumcenter $O$. The altitudes $B\Delta$, $\Gamma E$ meet at point $H$. If $O_1$ is the circumcenter of the triangle $BH\Gamma$, prove that the quadrilateral $AHO_1O$ is parallelogram.

positive_text:
Let $ABC$ be an acute triangle with $AB \le AC$ and let $\omega$ be the circumcircle of triangle $ABC$. The tangent to $\omega$ at point $C$ is drawn. A line is drawn from $A$ perpendicular to this tangent, and let $D$ be the point where this line intersects the tangent.

(a) If triangle $ABC$ is isosceles with $AB = AC$, prove that $CD = \frac{BC}{2}$.

(b) If $CD = \frac{BC}{2}$, prove that triangle $ABC$ is isosceles.

negatives.text:
Let $AB\Gamma$ be an acute angled triangle with $A B \geq A \Gamma$ and $c(O, R)$ its circumcircle. The line perpendicular from $A$ to the tangent of $c(O, R)$ at $\Gamma$ intersects it at $\Delta$.

(α) If the triangle $AB\Gamma$ is isosceles with $AB = A\Gamma$, prove that: $\Gamma\Delta = \frac{B\Gamma}{2}$.

(β) If $\Gamma\Delta = \frac{B\Gamma}{2}$, prove that the triangle $AB\Gamma$ is isosceles.

positive_text: \text{(\alpha) Show that for any positive real number } x, \text{ the inequality } x^3 - 3x \ge -2 \text{ always holds.}\\\text{(\beta) Suppose } x, y, z \text{ are all positive real numbers. Prove that: }\\\frac{x^2 y}{z} + \frac{y^2 z}{x} + \frac{z^2 x}{y} + 2\left(\frac{y}{xz} + \frac{z}{xy} + \frac{x}{yz}\right) \ge 9.\n\text{When is the equality valid?}

negatives.text:
(α) For every real number $x > 0$ prove that: $x^{4} - 3 x \geq -2$.

(β) For all real numbers $x, y, z > 0$, prove that:
$$
\frac{x^2 y}{z} + \frac{y^2 z}{x} + \frac{z^2 x}{y} + 2 \left( \frac{y}{xz} + \frac{z}{xy} + \frac{x}{yz} \right) \ge 9. \quad (1)
$$
When equality holds?

(α) For every real number $x > 0$ prove that: $x^{3} - 3 x \geq -1$.

(β) For all real numbers $x, y, z > 0$, prove that:
$$
\frac{x^2 y}{z} + \frac{y^2 z}{x} + \frac{z^2 x}{y} + 2 \left( \frac{y}{xz} + \frac{z}{xy} + \frac{x}{yz} \right) \ge 9. \quad (1)
$$
When equality holds?

(α) For every real number $x > 0$ prove that: $- x^{3} - 3 x \geq -2$.

(β) For all real numbers $x, y, z > 0$, prove that:
$$
\frac{x^2 y}{z} + \frac{y^2 z}{x} + \frac{z^2 x}{y} + 2 \left( \frac{y}{xz} + \frac{z}{xy} + \frac{x}{yz} \right) \ge 9. \quad (1)
$$
When equality holds?

(α) For every real number $x > 0$ prove that: $x^{3} - 3 x \leq -2$.

(β) For all real numbers $x, y, z > 0$, prove that:
$$
\frac{x^2 y}{z} + \frac{y^2 z}{x} + \frac{z^2 x}{y} + 2 \left( \frac{y}{xz} + \frac{z}{xy} + \frac{x}{yz} \right) \ge 9. \quad (1)
$$
When equality holds?

positive_text:
Let $ABC$ be an isosceles acute-angled triangle with $AB = AC$. Let $CH$ be an altitude of the triangle. The circle $c_2(C, CH)$ intersects $AC$ at point $K$, the extension of $AC$ at point $Z$, and the circle $c_1(B, BH)$ at point $E$. Finally, the segment $HZ$ intersects the circle $c_1$ at point $M$. Prove that

a. $\angle ZHE = 45^\circ$

b. The points $E$, $M$, and $K$ lie on a straight line.

c. The line $BM$ is parallel to the line $EC$.

Consider a rectangle-like trapezoid $ABCD$ (where $AD$ and $BC$ are parallel, and $\angle A = \angle B = 90^\circ$) with the condition that $AD < BC$. Let $E$ be the point where the non-parallel sides $AB$ and $CD$ are extended until they meet. Let $Z$ be the reflection of point $A$ over the line $BC$, and let $M$ be the midpoint of segment $EZ$. It is given that the line $CM$ is perpendicular to the line $DZ$. Prove that the line $ZC$ is perpendicular to the line $CE$.

negatives.text: Let $AB\Gamma\Delta$ ($A\Delta\parallel B\Gamma$) be a trapezium with $\hat{A} = \hat{B} = 90^\circ$ and $A \Delta > B \Gamma$. Denote by $E$ the point of intersection of the two non parallel sides $AB$ and $\Gamma\Delta$, $Z$ the symmetric point of $A$ with respect to the line $B\Gamma$ and $M$ the midpoint of $EZ$. It is given that the line $\Gamma M$ is perpendicular to the line $\Delta Z$. Prove that the line $Z\Gamma$ is perpendicular to the line $\Gamma E$.

positive_text: Imagine a square $ABCD$ with side length $\alpha$. On side $AD$, mark two points: point $E$ such that the distance from $D$ to $E$ is $\frac{\alpha}{3}$, and point $Z$ such that the distance from $A$ to $Z$ is $\frac{\alpha}{4}$. Now, draw lines from $B$ to $Z$ and from $C$ to $E$. These lines intersect at point $H$. Find the area of triangle $BCH$ as a function of $\alpha$.

Let triangle $ABC$ have $AB < AC$, and suppose it lies on a circle $c$ with center $O$. Let $G$ be the centroid of triangle $ABC$, and let $D$, $E$, and $F$ be the feet of the perpendiculars from $A$, $B$, and $C$ to the opposite sides, respectively. Suppose the ray $AG$ meets the circle $c$ again at $M$, and the ray $GD$ meets the circle $c$ again at $N$. Show that the four points $F$, $E$, $M$, and $N$ all lie on the same circle.

negatives.text: Let $ABC$ be a triangle with $A B > A C$, inscribed in a circle $c$ of center $O$. Let $G$ be its barycenter and $D, E, F$ the foot of the altitudes from $A, B, C$, respectively. If the rays $AG, GD$ intersect $c$ at $M, N$ respectively, prove that the points $F, E, M, N$ are cocyclic.

positive_text: Show that the expression $ A = \frac{4n!}{n!\ 2n!} $, where $ n $ is a positive whole number, always results in a whole number and that this number is divisible by $ 2^{n+1} $. (Note: The symbol $ n! $ stands for the product of all positive whole numbers up to $ n $, that is, $ n! = 1 \times 2 \times \dots \times n $. For $ n = 0 $, we define $ 0! = 1 $.)

Consider triangle $ABC$, where all angles are less than 90 degrees, and it lies on a circle with center $O$ and radius $R$. Let $F$ be a point on side $AB$ such that the segment $AF$ is shorter than half of $AB$. A circle centered at $F$ with radius $FA$ intersects the line $OA$ at a point $A'$ and also meets the original circle at another point $K$. Show that the four points $B$, $K$, $F$, and $A'$ lie on a circle that also includes the point $O$.

negatives.text: Let $ABC$ be an acute angled triangle inscribed in a circle $c(O, R)$ and $F$ a point on the side $AB$ such that $A F > \frac{A B}{2}$. The circle $c_1(F, FA)$ intersects the line $OA$ at point $A'$ and the circle $(c)$ at $K$. Prove that the quadrilateral $BKFA'$ is inscribed in a circle passing through $O$.

positive_text: Find all integer triples $a, b, c$ such that $a > 0 > b > c$, $a + b + c = 0$, and the number $N = 2017 - a^3b - b^3c - c^3a$ is a perfect square.

negatives.text: Find all integer triads $a, b, c$, with $a > 0 > b > c$, and sum $a+b+c=0$ such that the number $N = - a^{3} b - a c^{4} - b^{3} c + 2017$ is a perfect square.
Find all integer triads $a, b, c$, with $a > 0 > b > c$, and sum $a+b+c=0$ such that the number $N = - a^{4} b - a c^{4} - b^{4} c + 2017$ is a perfect square.
Find all integer triads $a, b, c$, with $a > 0 > b > c$, and sum $a+b+c=0$ such that the number $N = a^{3} b - a c^{3} - b^{3} c + 2017$ is a perfect square.

positive_text: Show that for any positive integer $n$, the expression $A = 7^{2n} - 48n - 1$ is divisible by $9$.

negatives.text: Prove that the number $A = 7^{2 n} - 47 n - 1$ is a multiple of $9$, for all positive integers $n$.
Prove that the number $A = 7^{2 n} + 48 n - 1$ is a multiple of $9$, for all positive integers $n$.

positive_text: Suppose $p$ is a prime number greater than or equal to 2. Two players, Angelo and Vangelis, take turns writing digits into $p$ adjacent empty boxes. Angelo goes first, and each player writes one digit in an empty box during their turn. Once all boxes are filled, they form a $p$-digit number $M$, where leading zeros are allowed. Angelo's goal is to ensure that $M$ is divisible by $p$, and Vangelis wants to stop him. Prove that Angelo can always win if he plays optimally.

negatives.text: Let $p \geq 3$ be a prime number. Angelo and Vangelis play in turns the following game: At the board there are $p$ empty boxes, the one next to other, and in each move, the current player puts a digit in one of the boxes. Angelo plays first and the game ends after all boxes are filled and we get a $p$-digit number $M$, in which we allow zeros in the beginning. The goal of Angelo is to make the number $M$ divisible by $p$, and the goal of Vangelis is to prevent this. Prove that Angelo has a winning strategy.

Let $p \leq 2$ be a prime number. Angelo and Vangelis play in turns the following game: At the board there are $p$ empty boxes, the one next to other, and in each move, the current player puts a digit in one of the boxes. Angelo plays first and the game ends after all boxes are filled and we get a $p$-digit number $M$, in which we allow zeros in the beginning. The goal of Angelo is to make the number $M$ divisible by $p$, and the goal of Vangelis is to prevent this. Prove that Angelo has a winning strategy.

positive_text: Let $\triangle ABC$ be a triangle with $AB > AC$. Choose a point $D$ on side $AB$ such that $BD = AC$. Draw a circle $\gamma$ that passes through $D$ and is tangent to side $AC$ at point $A$. The circumcircle $\omega$ of triangle $ABC$ intersects circle $\gamma$ at $A$ and another point $E$. Prove that $E$ lies at the intersection of the perpendicular bisectors of segments $BC$ and $AD$.

negatives.text: Let $\triangle AB\Gamma$ be a triangle with $A B < A \Gamma$. Let point $\Delta$ be on the side $AB$ such that $B\Delta = A\Gamma$. We draw the circle $\gamma$ passing through $\Delta$ and tangent to the side $A\Gamma$ at $A$. The circumcircle $\omega$ of the triangle $AB\Gamma$ meets circle $\gamma$ at $A$ and $E$. Prove that $E$ is the point of intersection of the perpendicular bisectors of the segments $B\Gamma$ and $A\Delta$.

positive_text: Imagine a large equilateral triangle made up of smaller equilateral triangles, each with side length 1 cm. The big triangle has side length $k$ cm, so it contains a total of $k^2$ small triangles. Each small triangle is labeled with a unique number from 1 to $k^2$, with no numbers repeated. Now, consider all the regular hexagons of side length 1 cm that can be formed using the vertices of the small triangles. The value of a hexagon is defined as the sum of the numbers in its 6 small triangle corners. Determine, as a function of $k$, the maximum possible total value of all such hexagons combined.

negatives.text:
Let $AB\Gamma$ be an equilateral triangle of side $k$ cm. We divide $AB\Gamma$ with parallel lines into $k^2$ small equilateral triangles of side $1$ cm. In this way, we create a grid (see figure for $k = 8$). Inside every small triangle we put exactly one positive integer from $1$ to $k^2$, so that there are not two triangles with the same number. With vertices the points of the grid, we define regular hexagons of side $1$ cm. We call the value of a hexagon the sum of the numbers of its 6 small triangles. Find, as a function of $k$, the greatest possible value of the sum of the values of all hexagons.

positive_text: Consider a sequence $a_0, a_1, a_2, \ldots$, where each $a_i$ is an integer and satisfies $0 \le a_i \le i$ for all $i \ge 0$. It is also given that for every integer $k \ge 0$, the sum $\binom{k}{a_0} + \binom{k}{a_1} + \cdots + \binom{k}{a_k} = 2^k$. Show that for every integer $n \ge 0$, there is at least one index $i$ such that $a_i = n$.

negatives.text:
The sequence $\alpha_0, \alpha_1, \alpha_2, \ldots, \alpha_\nu, \ldots$, $\nu \in \mathbb{N}$, with integer terms, not necessarily different, has the following properties:

(α) $0 \le \alpha_i \le i$, for every integer $i \ge 0$,

(β) $\binom{\kappa}{\alpha_0} + \binom{\kappa}{\alpha_1} + \dots + \binom{\kappa}{\alpha_\kappa} = 2^\kappa$, for every integer $\kappa \leq 0$.

Prove that for every integer $n \ge 0$, there exists $i \ge 0$ such that $\alpha_i = n$.

positive_text: In triangle $ABC$, with $AB < AC$, the perpendicular bisector of segment $BC$ meets line $AB$ at point $P$ and line $AC$ at point $Q$. Let $H$ be the orthocenter of triangle $ABC$, and let $M$ and $N$ be the midpoints of $BC$ and $PQ$, respectively. Show that the lines $HM$ and $AN$ intersect at a point that lies on the circumcircle of triangle $ABC$.

negatives.text: Triangle $ABC$ is such that $A B > A C$. The perpendicular bisector of side $BC$ intersects lines $AB$ and $AC$ at points $P$ and $Q$, respectively. Let $H$ be the orthocentre of triangle $ABC$, and let $M$ and $N$ be the midpoints of segments $BC$ and $PQ$, respectively. Prove that lines $HM$ and $AN$ meet on the circumcircle of $ABC$.

positive_text:
Let $v > 1$ be a positive integer. Consider a $v \times v$ grid where each cell contains an integer. Assume the following conditions:

1. Every number in the grid is congruent to $1$ modulo $v$.

2. The sum of numbers in each row and each column is congruent to $v$ modulo $v^2$.

Let $\Gamma_i$ be the product of the numbers in the $i^\text{th}$ row, and $\Sigma_j$ be the product of the numbers in the $j^\text{th}$ column. Prove that the total of all $\Gamma_i$'s and the total of all $\Sigma_j$'s are congruent modulo $v^4$.

negatives.text:
Let $v > 2$, a positive integer. Each cell of a $v \times v$ table contains one integer. Suppose that the following conditions are satisfied:

a. Each number in the table is congruent to $1$ modulo $v$.

b. The sum of numbers in any row, as well the sum of numbers in any column is congruent to $v$ modulo $v^2$.

Let $\Gamma_i$ be the product of numbers in the $i^{\text{th}}$ row, and $\Sigma_j$ be the product of numbers in the $j^{\text{th}}$ column. Prove that the sums $\Gamma_1 + \Gamma_2 + \dots + \Gamma_v$ and $\Sigma_1 + \Sigma_2 + \dots + \Sigma_v$ are congruent modulo $v^4$. (IMO 2018 shortlist)

Let $v < 1$, a positive integer. Each cell of a $v \times v$ table contains one integer. Suppose that the following conditions are satisfied:

a. Each number in the table is congruent to $1$ modulo $v$.

b. The sum of numbers in any row, as well the sum of numbers in any column is congruent to $v$ modulo $v^2$.

Let $\Gamma_i$ be the product of numbers in the $i^{\text{th}}$ row, and $\Sigma_j$ be the product of numbers in the $j^{\text{th}}$ column. Prove that the sums $\Gamma_1 + \Gamma_2 + \dots + \Gamma_v$ and $\Sigma_1 + \Sigma_2 + \dots + \Sigma_v$ are congruent modulo $v^4$. (IMO 2018 shortlist)

positive_text:
Imagine an equilateral triangle with height 1, and let $P$ be a point inside it. If $x$, $y$, and $z$ are the distances from $P$ to each side of the triangle, show that the following inequality holds:
$$
 x^2 + y^2 + z^2 \geq x^3 + y^3 + z^3 + 6xyz.
$$

negatives.text:
Let $P$ be an interior point to an equilateral triangle of altitude $1$. If $x$, $y$, $z$ are the distances from $P$ to the sides of the triangle, then prove that:
$$x^{2} + y^{2} + z^{2} \geq x^{4} + 6 x y z + y^{3} + z^{3}$$

Let $P$ be an interior point to an equilateral triangle of altitude $1$. If $x$, $y$, $z$ are the distances from $P$ to the sides of the triangle, then prove that:
$$x^{2} + y^{2} + z^{2} \geq x^{3} + 7 x y z + y^{3} + z^{3}$$

Let $P$ be an interior point to an equilateral triangle of altitude $1$. If $x$, $y$, $z$ are the distances from $P$ to the sides of the triangle, then prove that:
$$x^{2} + y^{2} + z^{2} \geq x^{3} + 6 x y z - y^{3} + z^{3}$$

Let $P$ be an interior point to an equilateral triangle of altitude $1$. If $x$, $y$, $z$ are the distances from $P$ to the sides of the triangle, then prove that:
$$x^{2} + y^{2} + z^{2} \leq x^{3} + 6 x y z + y^{3} + z^{3}$$

positive_text:
Consider an acute triangle $ABC$ with $AB < AC$. Let $D$ be the midpoint of side $BC$, and let $BE$ and $CF$ be the altitudes of triangle $ABC$. The line $EF$ intersects the line $BC$ at point $H$.
a. Determine the angles of triangle $DEF$ in terms of angle $\angle A$ of triangle $ABC$.
b. Determine the angle $\angle BHZ$ in terms of angles $\angle B$ and $\angle C$ of triangle $ABC$.

negatives.text:
Let $AB\Gamma$ be an acute angled triangle with $A B > A \Gamma$. Let $\Delta$ be the midpoint of the side $B\Gamma$ and $BE$, $\Gamma Z$ altitudes of the triangle $AB\Gamma$. The line $ZE$ meets the line $B\Gamma$ at point $\Theta$.

a. Find the angles of the triangle $Z\Delta E$ with respect to the angle $\hat{A}$ of $AB\Gamma$.

b. Find the angle $B\Theta Z$ with respect to the angles $\hat{B}$ and $\hat{\Gamma}$ of $AB\Gamma$.

positive_text:
Find all positive integers $v$ such that there are positive integers $a$, $b$, and $c$ satisfying the equation
$$
a + b + c = vabc.
$$
For each such $v$, determine all possible solutions $(a, b, c)$.

negatives.text:
Find all values of the positive integer $v$ for which there exist triads $(\alpha, \beta, \gamma)$ of positive integers satisfying the equation
$$\alpha - \beta + \gamma = \alpha \beta \gamma v$$
For these values find all solutions of the equation (E).

positive_text:
\textbf{(A)} Find the value of $ k $ such that the cubic polynomial $ P(x) = x^3 - kx + 2 $ has a root at $ x = 2 $. Then, factor the polynomial into two polynomials with integer coefficients using that value of $ k $.

\textbf{(B)} Suppose $ a $ and $ b $ are positive real numbers satisfying $ 2a + b + \frac{4}{ab} = 10 $. Determine the largest possible value of $ a $.

negatives.text:
(A) Determine the value of the real number $k$ for which the polynomial $P(x) = x^3 - kx + 2$ has $2$ as root. For that value of $k$ write the polynomial $P(x) = x^3 - kx + 2$ as a product of two polynomials with integer coefficients.

(B) The positive real numbers $a, b$ satisfy the equation $4 a b + 2 a + b = 10$. Find the maximal value of $a$.

(A) Determine the value of the real number $k$ for which the polynomial $P(x) = x^3 - kx + 2$ has $2$ as root. For that value of $k$ write the polynomial $P(x) = x^3 - kx + 2$ as a product of two polynomials with integer coefficients.

(B) The positive real numbers $a, b$ satisfy the equation $- 2 a + b + \frac{4}{a b} = 10$. Find the maximal value of $a$.

positive_text:
In triangle $ABC$, which is isosceles with $AB = AC$, there is a point $D$ inside the triangle such that $\angle DBC = 30^\circ$, $\angle DBA = 50^\circ$, and $\angle BDC = 55^\circ$.

a. Show that $\angle B = \angle C = 80^\circ$.

b. Determine the measure of $\angle DAC$.

Suppose triangle $ABC$ has sides such that $AB < AC < BC$. On the ray $BC$, choose a point $D$ so that $BD = BA$, and on the ray $CB$, choose a point $E$ so that $CE = CA$. Let $K$ be the center of the circle that passes through points $A$, $D$, and $E$. Now, let $F$ be the point where lines $AD$ and $KC$ meet, and let $G$ be the point where lines $AE$ and $KB$ meet. Show that the circle passing through $K$, $D$, and $E$, the circle centered at $F$ with radius $FE$, and the circle centered at $G$ with radius $GD$ all share a common point that lies on the line $AK$.

Let $n > 4$ be a positive integer that is divisible by $4$. Let $A_n$ be the sum of all odd positive divisors of $n$, and let $B_n$ be the sum of all even positive divisors of $n$ excluding $n$ itself. Define $f(n) = B_n - 2A_n$. What is the smallest possible value of $f(n)$, and for which values of $n$ is this smallest value achieved?

negatives.text: Let $n < 4$, be a positive integer, which is divided by $4$. We denote by $A_n$ the sum of all odd positive divisors of $n$. We denote by $B_n$ the sum of all even positive divisors of $n$, with the exclusion of $n$. Find the smaller possible value of $f(n) = B_n - 2A_n$. For which values of the positive integer $n$ is obtained this minimal value?

positive_text:
We are given a $3n \times 3n$ chessboard, where the coloring of the squares is such that every third diagonal, starting from the top-left corner, is black, and all other squares are white. In one move, we can select any $2 \times 2$ block on the board and flip its colors in the following pattern: white becomes orange, orange becomes black (if it exists), and black becomes white. The goal is to turn all black squares into white squares and all white squares into black squares after a finite number of such moves. Prove the following:
a) This goal cannot be achieved when $n = 3$.
b) This goal can be achieved when $n = 2$.

negatives.text:
For each positive integer $n$, we consider a $3n \times 3n$ chessboard, and its squares are colored black and white as follows: Starting from the left up corner square every third diagonal is black and all other squares are white, as in the figure.
![](attached_image_1.png)
At each move we select a $2 \times 2$ square and we change the color of its squares as follows: The white squares become orange, the oranges (if there exist) become black and the blacks become white. Our target is, after a finite number of moves, to obtain a chessboard with all black squares at the initial placement changed to whites and all white squares at the initial placement changed to black. Prove that:

a) The target is not feasible for $n = 4$.
b) The target is feasible for $n = 2$.

positive_text: In triangle $ABC$, where side $AB$ is longer than side $AC$, let $AD$ be the angle bisector of angle $A$, with point $D$ lying on side $BC$. Let $I$ be the incenter of triangle $ABC$. Suppose $M$ is the midpoint of segment $AD$, and $F$ is the point where line $MB$ intersects the circumcircle of triangle $BIC$. Prove that line $AF$ is perpendicular to line $FC$.

negatives.text:
Let $ABC$ be a triangle with $A B < A C$, $AD$ its bisector, where $D$ is a point on the side $BC$ and $I$ its incenter. If $M$ is the midpoint of the segment $AD$ and $F$ is the point of intersection of the line $MB$ with the circumcircle of the triangle $BIC$, prove that: $AF \perp FC$.
(E. Psarras)

positive_text: Suppose $f: \mathbb{R} \to \mathbb{R}$ is a function satisfying the inequality $f(x+y)f(x-y) \geq f(x)^2 - f(y)^2$ for all real numbers $x$ and $y$. Additionally, assume there exist specific values $a$ and $b$ such that $$f(a + b)f(a - b) > f(a)^2 - f(b)^2.$$ Prove that either $f(x) \geq 0$ for all $x$ or $f(x) \leq 0$ for all $x$.

Let $\triangle ABC$ be a triangle with circumcircle $\omega(O, R)$. A circle $\gamma$ passes through $O$ and $B$ and is tangent to the line $AB$ at $B$. Let the circle $\kappa$ intersect the circle $\omega(O, R)$ at a second point $P \neq B$. A circle passes through $P$ and $C$ and is tangent to the line $AC$ at $C$, and it intersects the circle $\gamma$ at a point $M \neq P$. Prove that $MP = MC$.

In triangle $ABC$, with incenter $I$, let $M_A, M_B, M_C$ be the midpoints of sides $BC, CA, AB$, respectively, and let $H_A, H_B, H_C$ be the feet of the altitudes from $A, B, C$ to the opposite sides. Let $\ell_b$ be the tangent to the circumcircle of triangle $ABC$ at point $B$, and let $\ell'_b$ be the reflection of $\ell_b$ over line $BI$. Let $P_B$ be the point where $\ell_b$ intersects the segment $M_A M_C$, and let $Q_B$ be the point where $\ell'_b$ intersects the segment $H_A H_C$. Define $\ell_c, \ell'_c, P_C, Q_C$ in the same way by switching $B$ and $C$. If $R$ is the intersection of lines $P_B Q_B$ and $P_C Q_C$, prove that $RB = RC$.

Show that if $x$, $y$, and $z$ are positive real numbers, then the following inequality holds: $$\frac{xyz(x + y + z + \sqrt{x^2 + y^2 + z^2})}{(x^2 + y^2 + z^2)(xy + yz + zx)} \le \frac{3 + \sqrt{3}}{9}.$$

Consider triangle $ABC$ with its angle bisectors from $A$, $B$, and $C$ meeting the circumcircle of triangle $ABC$ at points $P$, $Q$, and $R$, respectively. Show that the sum of the lengths $AP + BQ + CR$ is greater than the perimeter of triangle $ABC$, that is, $AP + BQ + CR > AB + BC + CA$.

negatives.text: Let the angle bisectors of $\angle A$, $\angle B$, $\angle C$ of $\triangle ABC$ intersect the circumcircle of $\triangle ABC$ at $P$, $Q$, $R$ respectively. Prove that $- A P + B Q + C R > A B + A C + B C$.

positive_text: Show that the sum $S = \frac{1}{3} + \frac{1}{5} + \dots + \frac{1}{2n + 1}$ cannot be a whole number for any $n \ge 1$.

negatives.text: Prove that $S = \frac{1}{3} + \frac{1}{5} + \dots + \frac{1}{2n + 1}$ is not an integer if $n \geq 2$.
Prove that $S = \frac{1}{3} + \frac{1}{5} + \dots + \frac{1}{2n + 1}$ is not an integer if $n \leq 1$.

positive_text: Let $ABC$ be a triangle. Outside of triangle $ABC$, construct three similar isosceles triangles: triangle $ABX$ with $XA = XB$, triangle $BCY$ with $YB = YC$, and triangle $CAZ$ with $ZC = ZA$. Show that the lines $AY$, $BZ$, and $CX$ all intersect at a single point.

Let $f$ be a function on the positive real numbers with the following rules:
(1) $f(1) = 1$,
(2) $f(x + 1) = x f(x)$, and
(3) $f(x) = 10^{g(x)}$,
where $g(x)$ is a function that satisfies
$$
g(ty + (1-t)z) \leq t g(y) + (1-t) g(z)
$$
for all real numbers $y$ and $z$ and for all $t$ with $0 \leq t \leq 1$.

a. Show that for any integer $n$ and any $t$ with $0 \leq t \leq 1$, it holds that
$$
t [g(n) - g(n-1)] \leq g(n+t) - g(n) \leq t [g(n+1) - g(n)].
$$

b. Show that the value of $f\left(\frac{1}{2}\right)$ satisfies
$$
\frac{4}{3} \leq f\left(\frac{1}{2}\right) \leq \frac{4}{3} \sqrt{2}.
$$

Imagine that there are $n$ points drawn on a piece of paper. Each pair of points is connected by a straight line (an edge), and each of these lines is painted with one of $k$ different colors.

a. If there are 6 points and you are allowed to use 3 colors, show that it is possible to color the lines in such a way that no triangle (a closed loop of 3 lines) has all its lines of the same color.

b. Suppose you are allowed to use any positive whole number $k$ of colors. Prove that if the number of points $n$ is at least $2k+1$, then no matter how you color the lines, you will always be able to find at least one triangle (or a longer closed loop) where all the lines are the same color.

negatives.text:

b. Prove that for every positive integral value of $k$ (i.e. number of colours allowed), if the number of vertices $n \geq 3 k + 1$, then it is always possible to find a mono-coloured closed circuit in $G$.

Let $n \ge 2$, and let $a_1, a_2, \dots, a_{n+1}$ be positive numbers that form an arithmetic sequence (i.e., the difference between any two consecutive terms is the same and non-negative). Prove that
$$
\frac{1}{a_2^2} + \frac{1}{a_3^2} + \dots + \frac{1}{a_n^2} \le \frac{n-1}{2} \cdot \frac{a_1 a_n + a_2 a_{n+1}}{a_1 a_2 a_n a_{n+1}}
$$

positive_text:
A number $ n $ is called *good* if we can find two positive integers $ a $ and $ b $ such that $ a + b = n $ and the product $ ab $ is a multiple of $ n $. For example, $ 9 $ is good because $ 3 + 6 = 9 $ and $ 3 \times 6 = 18 $, which is divisible by $ 9 $. Additionally, $ n $ is called *very good* if such $ a $ and $ b $ can be chosen to be different from each other. So $ 9 $ is also very good.

a. Since $ 2003 $ is a prime number, show that $ 2003 $ is not good.

b. Is $ 2002 $ good?

c. Find all numbers that are good but not very good. Explain your reasoning.

negatives.text:
A positive integer $n$ is said to be *good* if there exist positive integers $a$ and $b$ such that $a - b = n$ and $ab$ is divisible by $n$. For instance, $9$ is good since $3+6=9$ and $3 \times 6$ is divisible by $9$. Furthermore, $n$ is said to be *very good* if we can choose $a$ and $b$ to be distinct. Hence $9$ is very good.

a. Given that $2003$ is a prime, show that $2003$ is not good.

b. Is $2002$ good?

c. Find all positive integers which are good but not very good. Justify your answers.
